Overview

Divisional Head of Procurement & Procurement Business Partner

Location: United States, RemoteSalary: $143,901 – $197,864, depending on experience and qualifications. There may be flexibility for an exceptional candidate Preference for candidates based in or near the Northeast, with travel to company sites as required We’re looking for a senior procurement leader to take ownership of direct-material procurement across one of our divisions, while also connecting the business effectively with our Group Procurement team for indirect spend. This is a broad, hands-on leadership role. You’ll shape the divisional procurement strategy, strengthen how we manage suppliers and risk, and make sure group-led sourcing initiatives deliver results in practice, not just on a spreadsheet. The role is remote and can be based anywhere in the US. However, as many of our sites are in the Northeast, being based within reasonable reach of that region would be useful. You’ll need to travel to sites and suppliers when the work calls for it.

The role

You’ll lead and professionalise direct-material procurement across a complex, multi-site operation. That includes setting the strategy, building a clear pipeline of sourcing and cost-improvement activity, leading important supplier negotiations, and improving supply resilience.You’ll also act as the division’s main procurement business partner for indirect spend. You’ll make sure the division’s requirements are properly understood by Group Procurement and lead the local implementation of group agreements and category strategies. In short, you’ll help turn procurement plans into measurable business results.

Responsibilities

What you’ll do

  • Develop and run a divisional procurement strategy that supports commercial, operational and growth priorities.
  • Lead direct-material procurement across multiple sites, setting clear priorities, measures and ways of working.
  • Build and deliver category, commodity and supplier strategies covering cost, quality, delivery, service and resilience.
  • Create a prioritised pipeline of sourcing, negotiation, value-engineering and cost-improvement initiatives.
  • Lead strategic supplier negotiations, selection and contracting.
  • Work closely with engineering, operations, quality, R&D and supply chain on specifications, standardisation, substitution, new-product introduction and make-or-buy decisions.
  • Improve supplier performance through effective segmentation, relationship management and structured reviews.
  • Identify and manage supply risks such as single-source dependency, capacity constraints, supplier financial weakness and geographic concentration.
  • Put in place practical mitigation and continuity plans for critical materials and suppliers.
  • Represent the division with Group Procurement, making sure business needs, forecasts, specifications and operational constraints are clearly understood.
  • Coordinate divisional involvement in group sourcing projects, supplier evaluations and implementation plans.
  • Lead the adoption of group agreements, approved suppliers and purchasing channels across the division.
  • Track savings, cost avoidance, working-capital improvements and other benefits through to financial realisation, not just theoretical claims.
  • Strengthen procurement processes, systems, data, governance and commercial capability across the division.
  • Lead and develop procurement colleagues, creating clear accountability without adding bureaucracy for the sake of it

Qualifications

What you’ll bring

  • Significant procurement experience gained in a complex, multi-site or international organisation.
  • Strong direct-material procurement experience within manufacturing, engineering or a similar industrial environment.
  • A track record of developing and delivering category, commodity and supplier strategies.
  • Evidence that you’ve delivered procurement savings and successfully converted them into financially recognised business benefits.
  • Strong sourcing, negotiation, contracting and supplier-management experience.
  • Practical experience of managing supplier performance, continuity and supply-chain risk.
  • Experience working within a matrix or centre-led procurement model.
  • The confidence to influence senior stakeholders and challenge constructively, even when you don’t have direct authority.
  • Experience leading, developing and improving procurement teams.
  • Strong commercial, analytical and financial judgement.
  • A relevant degree, equivalent professional experience or both.
  • A recognised procurement qualification, such as CIPS, would be useful but isn’t essential.
You’ll be comfortable moving between strategy and delivery. One day you may be advising divisional leadership; the next, you may be working through a supplier risk or removing a barrier that’s stopping a new agreement from being adopted.You’ll also know that good procurement isn’t simply about pushing for the lowest price. It’s about balancing cost, quality, technical capability, delivery, innovation, resilience and sustainability, then making a decision the business can actually live with.

What you’ll get

  • A senior, high-visibility staff role with ownership across divisional direct and indirect procurement.
  • The opportunity to shape procurement strategy, capability and ways of working across a multi-site business.
  • A US-based remote working arrangement.
  • Travel to company sites and suppliers as required, with much of the site footprint located in the Northeast.
  • The chance to influence both divisional priorities and the wider global procurement agenda.

Interested in learning more?

If this sounds like the right next step, apply now.Don’t have an up-to-date CV? No problem. Apply with what you have, or reach out to our Talent team via LinkedIn for an initial conversation

Job Description:

Job Title: Senior Director, Procurement & Sourcing

Location: Remote | USA
Reports to: Chief Accounting Officer

Employment Type: Full-time

This is an existing vacancy

About the Role:

We’re seeking an experienced and strategic Director/Senior Director, Procurement & Sourcing to lead our global procurement function, with a focus on driving efficiency, governance, and value across our technology, software, and indirect spend categories. Reporting to the VP, Finance & FP&A, this leader will shape sourcing strategy, oversee vendor management, and partner closely with business and IT leaders to optimize spend across regions.

This role requires a mix of operational excellence, strategic negotiation, and stakeholder management, with an ability to navigate complex vendor ecosystems across North America and Europe.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop and execute the global procurement and sourcing strategy aligned with corporate objectives.
  • Lead sourcing for technology, software, and professional services, including enterprise systems, SaaS, and infrastructure contracts.
  • Build and manage relationships with key suppliers, ensuring competitive pricing, performance, and compliance.
  • Partner with IT, Finance, Legal, and Business Operations to optimize supplier lifecycle management and risk mitigation.
  • Establish category management frameworks and performance KPIs for cost, quality, and delivery.
  • Drive adoption of procurement best practices across regions, ensuring consistency while allowing local flexibility.
  • Oversee global RFP processes, contract negotiations, and renewal strategies.
  • Support procurement governance, supplier diversity initiatives, and ESG sourcing goals.
  • Mentor and develop a high-performing team of sourcing professionals.

Required Qualifications:

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in procurement, sourcing, or vendor management, including at least 5 years in a leadership role.
  • Proven experience managing global or multi-region procurement, ideally with exposure to European markets.
  • Strong background in IT/software procurement — SaaS, enterprise systems, licensing, and managed services.
  • Demonstrated success in contract negotiation, cost optimization, and supplier performance management.
  • Strategic thinker with excellent business acumen and strong cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Experience working in a fast-paced, technology-driven or global enterprise environment preferred.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Finance, or related field; MBA or professional certification (e.g., CPSM, CIPS) is an asset.

Compensation and Benefits

This position has a starting salary range of $207,000 - $267,000 USD per year. The range represents what we reasonably and in good faith expect to pay for the role at the time of posting. An employee’s pay within the range is determined by a number of factors, including relevant skills, education, qualifications, experience, performance, business or organizational needs, and geographic location.

Eligible employees may participate in medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, retirement savings programs, paid time off, wellness programs, and other company-sponsored benefits. Benefits vary by country and employment status.

Why Join JD Power

JD Power powers auto-related decisions through proprietary data, advanced analytics, deep industry expertise, and workflows that connect insight to action. Operating across North America, Europe, and Australia, we help customers make better decisions and achieve better outcomes.

As a virtual-first company, we offer flexible work arrangements, opportunities for learning and development, and a culture centered on the Values that guide how we work every day.

  • We power our customers’ success. Everything we do is focused on helping customers make better decisions and achieve better outcomes.
  • We are innovative, collaborative, and grounded in data. We combine advanced analytics with human expertise to deliver insight that holds up in the real world.
  • We make things easy. We turn complexity into clarity so teams can act faster and with confidence.
  • We get it done. We focus on execution, accountability, and results.
  • We start with trust and prove it every day. Independence, integrity, and credibility are the foundation of our work.

Equal Opportunity & Accommodations

JD Power is committed to employing a diverse workforce. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or disability.

JD Power is committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for individuals with disabilities or other protected needs under applicable local laws. Please contact for accommodation request.


Data Privacy

JD Power does not disclose your personal data to unauthorized third parties. However, as a global corporation consisting of multiple affiliated companies in various countries, JD Power has international sites and JD Power uses resources located throughout the world. JD Power may from time to time also use third parties to act on JD Power’s behalf. You agree to the fact that to the extent necessary your personal data may be transferred and/or disclosed to any company within JD Power group of companies as well as to third parties acting on JD Power’s behalf, including also transfers to servers and databases outside the country where you provided JD Power with your personal data. Such transfers may include for example transfers and/or disclosures outside the European Economic Area and in the United States of America. If you are a California or United Kingdom resident, additional disclosures about the information we collect and how we use that information can be found by clicking here.

Applications

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the country where employment is offered. JD Power does not provide employment sponsorship for this position.

This position is posted exclusively on and select trusted job boards such as LinkedIn or Indeed. All official communication comes from email addresses ending in @jdpower.com or @jdpa.com. We will never ask for payment, equipment purchases, or upfront fees. We may take additional steps to verify candidate information to protect the integrity of our recruitment process.

To all recruitment agencies: JD Power does not accept unsolicited agency resumes and we are not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Aerwave delivers next-generation Managed Wi-Fi for multifamily communities—seamless, gigabit-speed internet that’s always on, everywhere on your property.

With 24/7 domestic support, intuitive digital tools, and real-time insights, we empower residents, property teams, and owners to stay connected and in control. More than just Wi-Fi, Aerwave builds trust and future-proofs your community for tomorrow’s digital lifestyle.

The Circuit Procurement Lead is responsible for sourcing, negotiating, and managing telecommunications circuits that power managed Wi-Fi networks across multi-family residential communities (e.g., apartments, student housing, senior living). This role ensures every property has reliable, cost-effective, and scalable connectivity to support high-density resident usage, smart building technologies, and property operations.

RESPONSIBILITIES/ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Lead end-to-end procurement of internet circuits for multi-dwelling units (MDUs), including DIA, broadband, fiber, fixed wireless, and LTE/5G backup solutions.
  • Develop and manage relationships with telecom carriers, ISPs, aggregators, and local access providers.
  • Negotiate pricing, contracts, bulk agreements, and SLAs across portfolios of properties.
  • Evaluate circuit options based on property size, resident density, bandwidth demand, and building infrastructure.
  • Partner with network engineering and deployment teams to align circuit selection with Wi-Fi design standards for MDUs.
  • Coordinate circuit ordering, installation, and turn-up timelines for new property launches and existing site upgrades.
  • Maintain accurate inventory of all circuits, contracts, billing details, and renewal timelines.
  • Identify opportunities for bulk purchasing, cost reduction, and standardization across properties.
  • Monitor vendor performance, uptime, and SLA compliance, particularly for high-density environments.
  • Support escalation and resolution of circuit outages impacting residents and property operations.
  • Collaborate with property onboarding teams to ensure connectivity readiness prior to resident move-ins.
  • Track and forecast circuit demand for new developments, acquisitions, and expansions.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Telecommunications, Supply Chain, or related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 5+ years of experience in telecom procurement, circuit sourcing, or ISP/vendor management.
  • Strong understanding of high-density network requirements and circuit types (fiber, DIA, broadband, wireless failover).
  • Proven ability to negotiate telecom contracts and manage vendor relationships at scale.
  • Familiarity with bulk service agreements and multi-site procurement strategies.
  • Ability to translate property-specific needs into scalable connectivity solutions.
  • Excellent project management and organizational skills across multiple concurrent property deployments.
  • Strong analytical skills with a focus on cost optimization and performance tracking.
  • Experience with circuit inventory tools, billing systems, and procurement platforms.
  • Effective cross-functional communication with engineering, deployment, and property stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication and customer service skills.
  • Understand critical milestones that drive operational excellence.
  • Basic technical knowledge.
  • Proficiency in the use of a computer, and software applications including Microsoft Office.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Highly organized and attentive to detail, with the ability to work on multiple tasks/projects simultaneously (multi-task).
  • Effective interpersonal skills with the ability to work with personnel at all levels, both within and outside the company.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision on a highly productive team.
  • Ability to manage budgets, timelines, and resources effectively.
  • Easily takes initiative and works independently.
  • Maturity, professionalism, and good work ethic.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting multi-family housing, MDUs, or hospitality environments strongly preferred.
  • Experience with MikroTik & Ruckus.
  • Experience with managed WiFi networks.

Benefits:

  • Join a dynamic, fast-growing company where you will have the opportunity to make an immediate, high-level impact to Aerwave’s growth and success.
  • Clear line of sight for career advancement and significant accomplishments.
  • Base salary that is externally competitive and bonuses and ad-hoc recognition awards, that are based on efforts and tied to performance.
  • We work hard at Aerwave, and you will too. But that means we need time off to rest and recharge. All executive team members receive unlimited paid time off.
  • Additionally, you receive 15 paid Company holidays.
  • High-quality health care coverage through Aetna Base Plan. Aerwave covers 100% of the premium for the base plan and up to 75% of the premium of any higher-tier insurance plan.
  • 401(k) matching 100% up to 4% of base salary.
